definition_zh: 一次；曾经；一…就；一旦
definition_en: one single time; at some time in the past; as soon as; if ever, used to introduce a condition
core_image: 一枚只用过一次的票根，用过就被撕下丢进铁盒
scene: 抽屉最深处的铁盒里压着一张旧票根，边角磨得发白，纸上的字迹早已认不出。She once lived in this old house beside the river.
sceneCN: 这里 once 是「曾经、从前」（第 2 个义项：过去某个不确定的时期）；句意是她曾在这栋河边老屋里住过。画面是压着旧票根的铁盒与磨白的纸角。

derivatives.zh: 由 once 与 over 复合而成，义为「匆匆的一瞥；粗略的检查」
由 once 与 in a lifetime 组合而成，义为「一生只有一次的」

senses.title: One single time and no more
senses.definition: one time, and no more than one time
senses.definitionCN: 一次，而且仅只一次
senses.example: I met her once at a conference in Shanghai.
senses.exampleCN: 我在上海的一次会议上见过她一面。
senses.why: The Old English form was a genitive of the word for one, so the count starts at a single occasion and stops there.
senses.whyCN: 古英语形式是「一」这个词的属格，所以计数从单独一次开始，也就到此为止。

senses.title: At some time in the past
senses.definition: at an unspecified time in the past, especially a period that is now over
senses.definitionCN: 在过去某个不确定的时期，尤指已经结束的一段时光
senses.example: He once worked as a night guard in a paper mill.
senses.exampleCN: 他曾在造纸厂当过夜班保安。
senses.why: A single occasion placed far enough back in memory stops being a count and becomes a period that once existed, which is how the word turns into formerly.
senses.whyCN: 单独一次被推到记忆深处，就不再是计数，而成了曾经存在过的一段日子，词义于是转为「从前」。

senses.title: As soon as; at the moment that
senses.definition: as soon as something happens, something else happens or becomes true
senses.definitionCN: 某事刚一发生，另一件事就随之发生或成立
senses.example: Once the rain stopped, the whole street came out to dry its washing.
senses.exampleCN: 雨一停，整条街的人就出来晾衣服。
senses.why: The count shrinks to a single moment, and that moment of time becomes the hinge on which the next event turns.
senses.whyCN: 计数收窄到一个瞬间，而时间上的那一刻正成了下一件事转动的铰链。

senses.title: If ever; whenever a condition holds
senses.definition: used to introduce a condition: if something ever happens or is true, the main clause follows
senses.definitionCN: 用于引出条件：只要某事发生或成立，后面的结果就随之而来
senses.example: Once you sign the form, the offer cannot be withdrawn.
senses.exampleCN: 你一旦签了这张表，这个录用条件就不能撤回。
senses.why: From the moment that to provided that is a short step, because a single moment can also mark the point where a condition takes effect.
senses.whyCN: 从「就在那一刻」到「只要」只有一小步，因为单独的那一刻也可以标出条件开始生效的位置。

intro.en: Once is a frozen genitive of the Old English word for one, and it has kept the meaning of a single occasion for more than a thousand years.
intro.cn: once 是古英语「一」这个词属格形式的凝固，一千多年来一直保留「一次」的含义。

items.en: The numeral an meant one, and its genitive anes meant of one, which is the source of the modern word.
items.cn: 数词 an 意为「一」，它的属格 anes 意为「之一的」，正是现代 once 的来源。

items.en: In early English anes worked as an adverb for one time, and its final s was gradually absorbed into the spoken form.
items.cn: 在早期英语中，anes 作副词表示「一次」，词尾的 s 逐渐被口语形式吸收。

items.en: Middle English spellings such as ones and once competed, and once won because it matched the pattern of twice.
items.cn: 中古英语的 ones 与 once 等拼法并存，once 最终胜出，因为它与 twice 的构词方式相合。

items.en: By the sixteenth century once had also become a conjunction meaning as soon as, turning a count of times into a point in time.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，once 又发展出连词用法，表示「一…就」，把次数扩展为时间上的一个点。

items.en: Modern English keeps the adverb of counting and the conjunction of condition, and once also lives inside fixed phrases such as at once and once more.
items.cn: 现代英语保留计数的副词与表条件的连词，once 也活在 at once、once more 这类固定短语里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers other words built on the same count of one; the near-meaning group gathers words for a former time and for every time that something happens.
note.cn: 形近组收同样从「一」出发构成的词；近义组收表示从前某个时期以及每当某事发生时的词。

entries.definitionCN: 每当；无论何时。

entries.definition: Immediately at the moment that something happens.
entries.definitionCN: 一…就；在某事发生的那一刻。

normalIntro.en: The word is a frozen count of one, and its family keeps returning to a single occasion, a single past period and a single moment that starts something.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是「一」的凝固计数，同族用法反复回到单独一次、单独一段过去，以及开启某事的单独一刻。

normal.en: The Old English genitive anes meant of one, so once is literally a count of one occasion.
normal.cn: 古英语属格 anes 意为「之一的」，所以 once 字面上就是数一次。

normal.en: Once and twice share the ending -ce, which is why the two words sound like a matched pair.
normal.cn: once 与 twice 共用词尾 -ce，所以两个词听起来像成对的。

normal.en: At once means at one moment, and that is how a count turns into immediacy.
normal.cn: at once 意为「就在一刻」，计数就是这样转成「立刻」。

normal.en: Once as a conjunction marks the single moment when something begins, and English glosses it as as soon as.
normal.cn: once 作连词时标出某事开始的那一瞬间，英语用 as soon as 来解释它。

normal.en: For once stresses that the single occasion is unusual rather than the usual pattern.
normal.cn: for once 强调这一次不同寻常，而不是一贯如此。

abstract.en: Picture a ticket torn in half after one ride: the stub left in the box is the whole of the word once.
abstract.cn: 想象一张车票在一次行程后被撕成两半：留在盒里的票根就是 once 的全部含义。

abstract.en: A single second on a clock face can set everything else moving, and that second is once standing at the head of a clause.
abstract.cn: 钟面上单独的一秒能让之后的一切动起来，而这一秒就是站在小句开头的 once。

abstract.en: Memory turns one distant occasion into the softer word once, the way a photograph outlives the day it was taken.
abstract.cn: 记忆把遥远的一次变成语气更柔的 once，就像照片比拍摄的那一天活得更久。

definition_en: connected to or available through a computer network, especially the internet; as an adverb, by means of such a connection
core_image: 一根细线从桌上的机器伸向看不见的远方，屏幕随即亮起别人的声音
scene: 深夜的书房里只剩屏幕的光，桌角那根网线轻轻闪着小灯。She bought the tickets online and printed them at home.
sceneCN: 这里 online 是「在网上、联网地」（第 2 个义项：通过互联网进行某种活动）；句意是她在网上买了票，又在家打印出来。画面是深夜的书房、亮着的屏幕与闪烁的网线指示灯。

derivatives.zh: 由表示「离开」的 off 与 line 复合，与 online 构成反义对，义为「离线的」

senses.title: Connected to a computer network
senses.definition: connected to a computer network or to the internet and able to exchange data
senses.definitionCN: 接入计算机网络或互联网，能够交换数据
senses.example: The printer is online, so the file went straight to paper.
senses.exampleCN: 打印机已联网，文件直接就印到了纸上。
senses.why: Line first named a wire or a telephone connection, so being on that line is literally being attached to the network.
senses.whyCN: line 最初指一根导线或一条电话线，所谓「在这条线上」就是实实在在接在网络里。

senses.title: By means of an internet connection
senses.definition: by using an internet connection rather than a physical place or a paper form
senses.definitionCN: 借助互联网连接，而不是通过实体场所或纸质表格
senses.example: She bought the tickets online and printed them at home.
senses.exampleCN: 她在网上买了票，又在家打印出来。
senses.why: Once the line carries data, any action done through it can take the same word as an adverb of manner.
senses.whyCN: 当这条线传输的是数据，任何经由它完成的动作都能用同一个词作方式状语。

senses.title: Available or stored on the internet
senses.definition: existing, offered or stored on the internet, as opposed to a printed or physical version
senses.definitionCN: 存在于互联网上、在网上提供或保存的，与纸质或实体版本相对
senses.example: The journal moved its whole archive online last year.
senses.exampleCN: 这家期刊去年把全部过刊搬到了网上。
senses.why: The adjective then moves from the connected machine to the thing that can only be reached through that connection.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词于是从「联网的机器」转到「只能通过网络抵达的内容」。

intro.en: Online joins the old noun line with the preposition on, and its modern life began with telephone wires before it passed to computer networks.
intro.cn: online 把古老的名词 line 与介词 on 合在一起，它的现代生命先始于电话线，随后转到计算机网络。

items.en: Linea meant a thread of flax and then any straight cord, and it is the source of the English noun line.
items.cn: linea 原指一根亚麻线，后来泛指任何笔直的绳索，是英语名词 line 的来源。

items.en: Old English borrowed line for a rope or a cord, and the word later also meant a row and a boundary.
items.cn: 古英语借入 line 表示绳索，这个词后来又指一排、一行以及一条界线。

items.en: In the nineteenth century a line was the wire joining two telephones, and being on the line meant being connected.
items.cn: 十九世纪，line 指连接两台电话的导线，「在线上」就意味着接通。

items.en: With computer networks the line became a data connection, and online was formed for equipment attached to it.
items.cn: 到了计算机网络时期，这条线变成数据连接，online 随之造出，用来形容接入其中的设备。

items.en: Modern English extends online from the connected device to the activity performed through it and to the content kept there.
items.cn: 现代英语把 online 从「接通的设备」扩展到「经由它完成的活动」与「存放在其中的内容」。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the opposite form and other compounds built on line; the near-meaning group gathers words about networks and electronic access.
note.cn: 形近组收它的反义形式以及同样以 line 构成的复合词；近义组收表示网络与电子访问的词。

entries.definitionCN: 形状的外缘或简要提纲；同含 line，但不表示连接。

entries.definition: Joined to a network or to another device.
entries.definitionCN: 接入网络或与另一设备相连的。

entries.definition: Stored or carried as electronic data rather than on paper.
entries.definitionCN: 以电子数据而非纸质方式存储或传输的。

entries.definition: Existing on computers or networks rather than in a physical place.
entries.definitionCN: 存在于计算机或网络中而不是实体场所的。

entries.definition: Accessed from a distance, usually through a network.
entries.definitionCN: 从远处访问的，通常经由网络。

normalIntro.en: The word pictures a machine attached to a line, and its family keeps the same thin thread running between a room and the world outside.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词描绘一台接在一条线上的机器，同族用法始终保留那根从房间伸向外界的细线。

normal.en: Line came from Latin linea, a thread, so online inherits the picture of a cord.
normal.cn: line 来自拉丁语 linea（线），所以 online 继承了「一根绳线」的画面。

normal.en: On adds the idea of being attached to or supported by that cord.
normal.cn: on 加上「附着于、由它支撑」的意思。

normal.en: Offline replaces on with off and marks a machine that has stepped away from the network.
normal.cn: offline 用 off 替换 on，标出已经离开网络的机器。

normal.en: Telephone lines gave the word its first everyday use, long before computers arrived.
normal.cn: 电话线给了这个词最早的日常用法，远在计算机出现之前。

normal.en: Online course and online shopping show the same word spreading to study and to trade.
normal.cn: online course 与 online shopping 说明同一个词又扩展到了学习与买卖。

abstract.en: Picture a single cable running out of a lit room into the dark: whatever waits at the other end becomes present on the screen.
abstract.cn: 想象一根线从亮着灯的屋子伸进黑暗：另一头的一切都会出现在屏幕上。

abstract.en: Being online means the walls of the room no longer decide what you can reach.
abstract.cn: 「在线」意味着房间的墙不再决定你能触及什么。

abstract.en: The same word covers the wire, the act and the content, because a connection quietly turns into a place.
abstract.cn: 同一个词覆盖了线路、动作与内容，因为一条连接会悄悄变成一个场所。

examples.en: She bought the tickets online and printed them at home.
examples.cn: 她在网上买了票，又在家打印出来。

examples.en: The printer is online, so the file went straight to paper.
examples.cn: 打印机已联网，文件直接就印到了纸上。

examples.en: Most of the course materials are now online.
examples.cn: 大部分课程材料现在都在网上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，来网」——哦，网来了，人就上线了；online 意为在线的、上网的。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a machine attached to a line; the senses move from the connected device to the action performed through it and to the material kept there.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「接在一条线上的设备」；义项从设备本身，转到经由它完成的活动，再到存放在线上的内容。

branches.cn: 打印机上的小灯转绿

definition_en: and nothing or nobody else; no more than; single and without a second one; but, used to introduce a drawback
core_image: 一排同样的杯子被逐个搬走，只有一个留在原来的位置
scene: 仓库清点那天，货架上成排的水杯被一件件搬走，最后只剩一只留在原来的位置。Only one cup was left on the shelf after the count.
sceneCN: 这里 only 是「唯一的、仅剩的」（第 2 个义项：同类中只有一个）；句意是清点之后货架上只剩一只杯子。画面是空了大半的货架与孤零零的一只杯子。

derivatives.zh: 由 only 与 child 组成的固定说法，义为「独生子女」
由 only 与 begotten 复合而成的古语，义为「独生的；唯一的」
由 only 的词基 one 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「一体；同一性」

senses.title: No more than; and nothing else
senses.definition: no more than a particular number, amount or thing, and nothing in addition
senses.definitionCN: 不超过某个数目、数量或事物，此外再无别的
senses.example: She packed only a small bag for the whole week.
senses.exampleCN: 整整一周她只收拾了一个小包。
senses.why: The word is one plus -ly, and its job is to cut a set down to a single member, so the sense begins as a limit on quantity.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 one 加 -ly 构成，职责是把一个集合削减到单独一个成员，所以词义从「限量」开始。

senses.title: Single and without another
senses.definition: being the single one of its kind, with no second one to choose from
senses.definitionCN: 同类之中只有一个，没有第二个可供选择
senses.example: Only one cup was left on the shelf after the count.
senses.exampleCN: 清点之后，货架上只剩一只杯子。
senses.why: When the same limit is applied to a whole group, the member left is the sole one, and the adverb turns into an adjective of uniqueness.
senses.whyCN: 把同样的限量用在整个群体上，剩下的那一个就成了唯一者，副词于是变成表「唯一」的形容词。

senses.title: Solely, marking the single person or thing that qualifies
senses.definition: used to say that a particular person or thing is the only one that does something or is allowed to do it
senses.definitionCN: 用来说明某人或某物是唯一做某事或获准做某事的一个
senses.example: Only the manager can open that safe.
senses.exampleCN: 只有经理才能打开那个保险柜。
senses.why: Here the cut falls on the doers rather than on the quantity, so the word points at the single agent allowed to act.
senses.whyCN: 这里的削减落在做事的人而不是数量上，所以这个词指向唯一获准行动的那个主体。

senses.title: But; except that
senses.definition: used before a fact that makes what was just said less strong or less happy
senses.definitionCN: 用在某个使前文减弱或令人不那么愉快的事实之前
senses.example: The flat is cheap, only it is far from the station.
senses.exampleCN: 这套房子便宜，只不过离车站太远。
senses.why: A limit on goodness is still a limit, so the same cutting word comes to mark the one flaw that a praise has to admit.
senses.whyCN: 对「好处」加以限制仍然是限制，于是这个表示削减的词转来标出称赞不得不承认的那一处缺陷。

intro.en: Only is one plus the suffix -ly, and it grew from a numeral into a word that limits, singles out and finally concedes.
intro.cn: only 由「一」加后缀 -ly 构成，从数词长成一个表示限量、挑出唯一者、最后表示让步的词。

items.en: The adjective anlic meant one-like or alone, built from an, one, and -lic, the ancestor of -ly.
items.cn: 形容词 anlic 意为「像一的、单独的」，由 an（一）与 -lic（-ly 的前身）构成。

items.en: The adverb anlice limited a statement to a single item, and its spoken form gradually shrank toward only.
items.cn: 副词 anlice 把陈述限制在单独一项上，它的口语形式逐渐缩减为 only。

items.en: Middle English only served both as adjective and adverb, meaning alone, single and no more than.
items.cn: 中古英语的 only 兼作形容词与副词，意为单独的、唯一的、仅仅。

items.en: Later the word gained a concessive use before clauses of objection, as in it is cheap, only it is far.
items.cn: 后来这个词又在表示异议的小句前获得让步用法，如「便宜，只不过太远」。

items.en: Modern English uses only for quantity, for uniqueness, for a single qualifying person, and for a mild objection.
items.cn: 现代英语用 only 表示数量限制、唯一性、唯一符合条件者，以及温和的反对。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same one-plus-suffix pattern; the near-meaning group gathers words of limitation and singleness.
note.cn: 形近组收同样由「一」加后缀构成的词；近义组收表示限制与单独的词语。

entries.definitionCN: only 内部那个数词，至今表示单独的一件或一人。

entries.definition: Built in origin on the same one-plus pattern, meaning without others.
entries.definitionCN: 来源上同样由「一」加后缀构成，意为独自、没有别人。

entries.definition: Another adverb built from one, meaning one time; it sounds close but marks a count rather than a limit.
entries.definitionCN: 同样由「一」构成的副词，意为一次；读音相近，但标的是次数而非限量。

entries.definition: Only and nothing more, used to play down what is described.
entries.definitionCN: 仅仅、只不过，用来淡化所描述的事物。

entries.definition: Exactly, or only; often interchangeable with only in limits.
entries.definitionCN: 恰好、仅仅；在表示限制时常可与 only 互换。

entries.definition: For one reason or by one person alone.
entries.definitionCN: 仅仅因为一个原因，或只由一个人。

entries.definition: Single and the only one existing.
entries.definitionCN: 单独的；唯一存在的。

normalIntro.en: The word leaves a single item in view, and its family keeps narrowing a shelf, a group and a sentence down to one member.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词只把一个物件留在视野里，同族用法一再把货架、群体与句子收窄到一个成员。

normal.en: Only is one plus -ly, so its oldest job is to leave a single item in view.
normal.cn: only 是 one 加 -ly，最古老的任务就是只留一个物件在视野里。

normal.en: Alone and lonely share the same one-plus-suffix origin, which is why all three suggest being by oneself.
normal.cn: alone 与 lonely 共用「一」加后缀的来源，所以三者都带「独自」的意味。

normal.en: Only the manager limits the doers, while only a small bag limits the quantity.
normal.cn: only the manager 限制的是做事的人，only a small bag 限制的是数量。

normal.en: Not only opens a set instead of closing it, which is why it pairs with but also.
normal.cn: not only 不是关上一个集合，而是把它打开，所以要与 but also 配合。

normal.en: The concessive only, as in only it is far, marks the single flaw left in a praise.
normal.cn: 表示让步的 only，如 only it is far，标出称赞里剩下的那一处缺陷。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf of identical cups and all but one carried away: the survivor is the thing only points at.
abstract.cn: 想象一货架同样的杯子只只被搬走，只剩一只：留下来的那只就是 only 所指的东西。

abstract.en: A spotlight narrowed to one face explains the word better than a definition, because everything else simply falls outside the beam.
abstract.cn: 把聚光灯收窄到一张脸上，比任何定义都更能解释这个词，因为其余一切都落在光束之外。

abstract.en: The same narrowing falls on a number, a person or a good quality, which is why one small word serves four jobs.
abstract.cn: 同一种收窄可以落在数量、某个人或某处好处上，所以这一个小词能担四项职责。

definition_zh: 操作；运转；经营；动手术
definition_en: to work or function, to control a machine, to run a business, or to perform a medical operation
core_image: 一只手按下按钮，整排机器依次发出低响，像身体里某处重新开始供血
scene: 深夜的泵房里，值班员按下启动键，旧水泵先抖了两下，随后平稳地响了起来。The old pump began to operate smoothly after the valve was replaced.
sceneCN: 这里是「运转」（第 1 个义项：机器或系统开始工作并保持运行）；句意为换过阀门之后，旧水泵开始平稳运转。图中可辨识物件：泵房管道、启动键、压力表。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语过去分词词干加 -tion 构成，义为「操作；手术；运算」
由拉丁语 operator（干活的人）进入英语，义为「操作员；运算符」
由 operari 加 -ive 构成，义为「起作用的；实施中的」

senses.title: To work or run
senses.definition: to work or function, especially of a machine, system or service
senses.definitionCN: 尤指机器、系统或服务在工作、起作用
senses.example: The heating system operates at low cost in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 这套供暖系统冬天运行成本很低。
senses.why: Latin operari means to work, so a machine that runs is the old idea of working moved from a person onto a device.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 operari 意为「干活」，机器在运行这个义项，就是把「干活」从人身上挪到了装置上。

senses.title: To control a machine
senses.definition: to control or use a machine, vehicle or piece of equipment
senses.definitionCN: 控制并使用机器、车辆或设备
senses.example: Only trained staff may operate the crane.
senses.exampleCN: 只有受过训练的人员才能操作这台起重机。
senses.why: If a machine can work by itself, a person can also make it work, and the transitive use simply adds a hand on the controls.
senses.whyCN: 机器既然能自己运行，人也能使它运行；及物用法只是在「干活」这件事上多了一只放在操纵杆上的手。

senses.title: To perform surgery
senses.definition: to cut into a patient's body in order to treat a disease or an injury
senses.definitionCN: 切开病人身体以治疗疾病或损伤
senses.example: Surgeons operated on her knee at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 外科医生在黎明时为她做了膝关节手术。
senses.why: Surgery is skilled work done with the hands on the body, so the general verb for working took the medical sense through the phrase operate on.
senses.whyCN: 手术是靠双手在身体上完成的技艺活，于是「干活」这个泛用动词借着 operate on 这个说法，担起了医学含义。

senses.title: To run a business or organization
senses.definition: to manage or run a business, service or organization
senses.definitionCN: 管理或经营一项生意、服务或组织
senses.example: The charity operates three shelters in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 这家慈善机构在市内经营三家收容所。
senses.why: Running an organization is continuous work, so the same verb moves from a single machine to a whole enterprise.
senses.whyCN: 经营一个组织是持续不断的活，同一个动词就这样从一台机器扩大到整个机构。

intro.en: Operate comes straight from Latin, where a verb for working gave English both the verb and its nouns; it is not the same word as opera, which arrived through Italian.
intro.cn: operate 直接从拉丁语进入英语，那里一个意为「干活」的动词为英语提供了动词和它的名词；它与经意大利语而来的 opera 不是同一个词。

items.en: Latin opus named work or a product, and its genitive operis supplied the stem for the verbs of working.
items.cn: 拉丁语 opus 指工作或成果，属格 operis 为表示「干活」的一系列动词提供了词干。

items.en: Operari was a deponent verb meaning to work, to labor or to produce an effect.
items.cn: operari 是一个异态动词，意为干活、劳作或产生作用。

items.en: Its past participle operatus meant having worked, and this is the form English took when it borrowed the verb.
items.cn: 它的过去分词 operatus 意为「已经干过」，英语借入动词时带的就是这个形式。

items.en: Early English operate meant to produce an effect or to exert force, a sense still heard in the word operation.
items.cn: 早期的英语 operate 意为产生效果或施加力量，这层意思至今还能在 operation 里听到。

items.en: Modern English widened operate to machines, businesses and surgery while keeping the older sense of having an effect.
items.cn: 现代英语把 operate 扩展到机器、企业和手术，同时保留了「起作用」这层旧义。

note.en: The look-alike group is the Latin-derived working family; the near-meaning group is everyday verbs for running or handling something.
note.cn: 形近组是由拉丁语「干活」长出的词族；近义组是日常里表示运转或摆弄某物的动词。

entries.definition: The act of working, or a medical procedure.
entries.definitionCN: 运作的行为，或医疗手术。

entries.definition: Working, or used for working, as in an operating system.
entries.definitionCN: 运转的或用于运转的，如操作系统。

entries.definition: A person who works a machine or handles telephone calls.
entries.definitionCN: 操作机器或处理电话的人。

entries.definition: Working or in force, and also a person who carries out secret work.
entries.definitionCN: 起作用的、实施中的，也指从事秘密工作的人。

entries.definition: To make a machine or a business work.
entries.definitionCN: 使机器或企业运转。

entries.definition: To work in the normal or expected way.
entries.definitionCN: 以正常或预期的方式工作。

entries.definition: To use or control something with the hands.
entries.definitionCN: 用手使用或控制某物。

normalIntro.en: Everything in this family goes back to the Latin verb for working, so the mnemonics follow the work from hands to machines to bodies.
normalIntro.cn: 这一族词都可追到拉丁语表示「干活」的动词，所以联想沿着「活」从双手走到机器，再到身体。

normal.en: Operari means to work, so operate is first of all to be busy doing something.
normal.cn: operari 意为干活，所以 operate 首先是「在忙着做某事」。

normal.en: Operation adds -tion and turns the working into a thing you can name.
normal.cn: operation 加 -tion，把「干活」变成一个可以叫出名字的东西。

normal.en: Operator adds -or and turns the working into the person who does it.
normal.cn: operator 加 -or，把「干活」变成干活的那个人。

normal.en: Operate on is the medical phrase, where the body is the thing being worked on.
normal.cn: operate on 是医学说法，被「干活」的对象就是身体。

normal.en: Operative means still at work, which is why a spy is also called one.
normal.cn: operative 意为仍在起作用，这就是特工也被叫作 operative 的原因。

abstract.en: A hand on a lever is the shortest picture of operate: effort passing into a machine.
abstract.cn: 一只手搭在操纵杆上，就是 operate 最短的画面：力气传进机器。

abstract.en: A machine that runs is a person's work continuing after the person has stepped away.
abstract.cn: 机器自己转着，就是人的活在离开之后还继续着。

abstract.en: Cutting a body to mend it shows how far the plain word for working can travel.
abstract.cn: 切开身体去修补它，说明「干活」这个平常词能走多远。

examples.en: The old pump began to operate smoothly after the valve was replaced.
examples.cn: 换过阀门之后，旧水泵开始平稳运转。

examples.en: Only trained staff may operate the crane.
examples.cn: 只有受过训练的人员才能操作这台起重机。

examples.en: The charity operates three shelters in the city.
examples.cn: 这家慈善机构在市内经营三家收容所。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，怕累他」——机器开动以后，最怕累坏那个守着它的人；记住 operate 是操作、运转。

root: 拉丁语 opus（工作、成果）派生动词 operari（干活、起作用），过去分词 operatus 进入英语成为 operate；同族词有 operation、operator、operative、operating。opera 虽与它共享更远的拉丁词根，却经意大利语而来、指「歌剧」，不能与 operate 混用。

sensesIntro.en: The core is work being done; the senses move from a machine running, to a hand controlling it, to surgery, and finally to running a whole enterprise.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「正在干的活」；义项从机器自己运行，移到人伸手操纵，再到在身体上动刀，最后到经营整个机构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pressing a button and a row of machines answering with a low hum.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手按下按钮，一排机器用低沉的声音回应。

branches.en: a pump finding its rhythm after a repair
branches.cn: 修好之后水泵重新找到节奏

branches.en: an operator guiding a crane over a roof
branches.cn: 操作员把起重机吊过屋顶

branches.en: a trainee learning to keep both hands still
branches.cn: 学徒练习让两只手保持不动

branches.en: a lamp above a table in a quiet room
branches.cn: 安静房间里，台面上方的一盏灯

branches.en: a small office counting the shelters it runs
branches.cn: 小办公室清点自己经营的那几家收容所

intro.en: The word is a Latin participle turned English verb, and the family adds -tion for the act, -or for the person and -ive for the working quality.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语分词变成的英语动词；同族词用 -tion 表示行为，用 -or 表示人，用 -ive 表示「起作用的」性质。

latinIntro.en: The Latin behind operate is the working branch of the opus family: the verb, its participle and the agent noun.
latinIntro.cn: operate 背后的拉丁语是 opus 一族里「干活」的那一支：动词、分词和施事名词。

definition_zh: 运转；操作；手术；行动；业务；运算；经营单位
definition_en: the working of a machine or system, a planned activity, a surgical treatment, or a mathematical process
core_image: 手术灯下，主刀医生的手停在心脏上方，旁边屏幕上跳动着体外循环机的运行曲线
scene: 手术灯亮起后，主刀医生用两个小时完成了孩子心脏上的一处修补。The hospital performed a delicate operation on the child's heart that morning.
sceneCN: 句中的说法指「在身体上施行的外科手术」（第 3 个义项：由医生切开或进入体内完成的治疗）；句意为那天上午医院为孩子的心脏做了一台精细手术。图中可辨识物件：手术灯、体外循环机、监护屏、无菌手套；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 行动；业务；经营单位（可数）

senses.title: The working of a machine or system
senses.definition: the way in which a device, plant or system performs its function
senses.definitionCN: 装置、工厂或系统发挥功能的方式
senses.example: The pump's operation is monitored from a control room.
senses.exampleCN: 泵的运转由控制室监控。
senses.why: The word rests on a Latin verb meaning to work, so the working of a system is its most literal sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建立在拉丁语「工作」动词之上，因此系统的运转是它最字面的义项。

senses.title: The act of making a device work
senses.definition: the act of running or controlling a machine by hand or by control
senses.definitionCN: 用手或控制装置使机器运行的动作
senses.example: Operation of the crane requires two trained hands.
senses.exampleCN: 操作这台吊车需要两名受过训练的人。
senses.why: Doing the work and making something else work are two sides of one verb, so the act of driving a machine took the same noun.
senses.whyCN: 自己干活与让别的东西干活是同一个动词的两面，因此驱动机器的动作也用了这个名词。

senses.title: A surgical treatment
senses.definition: a treatment in which a surgeon cuts into or enters the body to repair it
senses.definitionCN: 外科医生切开或进入体内进行修补的治疗
senses.example: The operation on her knee lasted two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 她膝盖的手术持续了两个小时。
senses.why: Surgery is work done on a body, so medicine used the general noun for work and it became the everyday word for an intervention.
senses.whyCN: 手术是对身体所做的工作，因此医学用这个泛指「工作」的名词，它后来成了介入治疗的日常说法。

senses.title: A planned military action
senses.definition: an organized movement of forces with a set aim, usually given a name
senses.definitionCN: 有明确目标、通常有代号的部队组织行动
senses.example: The rescue operation began at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 救援行动在黎明开始。
senses.why: Military staffs speak of work done by combined forces as one operation, and the sense spread to any coordinated action.
senses.whyCN: 军事参谋把多支部队合力完成的工作称为一次行动，这个义项后来扩展到任何协同行动。

senses.title: The everyday activities of a business
senses.definition: the routine activities by which a company or institution keeps running, usually in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 公司或机构维持运转的日常活动，常用复数
senses.example: The firm moved its operations closer to the port.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司把业务迁到离港口更近的地方。
senses.why: A business is a set of workings, so its routine activities are called its operations rather than its plans.
senses.whyCN: 一家企业就是一组运转，因此它的日常活动被称为业务，而不是计划。

senses.title: A mathematical process
senses.definition: a rule applied to numbers or symbols to produce a new value
senses.definitionCN: 施于数字或符号以得出新值的规则
senses.example: Addition is the first operation children learn.
senses.exampleCN: 加法是孩子学的第一种运算。
senses.why: Mathematics treats each rule as work performed on symbols, which is the same idea of a working applied to numbers.
senses.whyCN: 数学把每条规则看作对符号所做的工作，这与「运转」是同一个意思，只是对象换成数字。

senses.title: A running business or unit
senses.definition: an enterprise or a distinct unit that is being run as a going concern
senses.definitionCN: 作为持续经营体运作的企业或独立单位
senses.example: The mine is a profitable operation.
senses.exampleCN: 这座矿是一个盈利的经营单位。
senses.why: Once a business is seen as something that works, the thing that works can itself be called an operation.
senses.whyCN: 一旦企业被看作在运转的东西，这个在运转的东西本身就可以被称为一个经营单位。

senses.title: An organized piece of work with a plan
senses.titleCN: 有组织的行动；专项行动
senses.definition: a coordinated piece of work, often large, carried out by a group toward one aim
senses.definitionCN: 由一群人朝同一目标实施的、常具规模的协同工作
senses.example: The cleanup operation involved three hundred volunteers.
senses.exampleCN: 这次清理行动动用了三百名志愿者。
senses.why: Any large piece of coordinated work can be called an operation, because it is work organized as one working whole.
senses.whyCN: 任何大规模协同工作都可称为一次行动，因为它被组织成一个整体的运作。

intro.en: Operation came through Old French from Latin operatio 'a working', built on operari 'to work' and opus 'work'. The origin of opus before Latin is unsettled. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词经古法语来自拉丁语表示「工作」的名词，其基础为表示「工作」的动词与名词。名词词根在拉丁语之前的来源没有定论。年代均为约数。

items.en: Opus meant 'work, a piece of work, a task'. Its pre-Latin origin is not established, and the root sometimes proposed for it is a reconstruction, so source uncertain at that depth.
items.cn: opus 意为「工作、一件作品、任务」。其在拉丁语之前的来源未获证明，有时为它提出的词根属重构形式，故更深一层来源不确定。

items.en: Operari, a deponent verb, meant 'to work, to labour, to perform'.
items.cn: operari 是一个异态动词，意为「工作、劳作、施行」。

items.en: Operatio, from operari plus the noun suffix -io, named a working or the result of working.
items.cn: operatio 由 operari 加名词后缀 -io 构成，指工作这一动作或其结果。

items.en: Old French brought the noun into English in the fourteenth century, first for any action or effect.
items.cn: 古法语在十四世纪把这个名词带入英语，最初指任何动作或效果。

items.en: From the seventeenth century surgery adopted the word for an intervention, and from the eighteenth military staffs used it for a named action.
items.cn: 十七世纪起外科把这个词用于介入治疗，十八世纪起军事参谋用它指有代号的行动。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same Latin noun of work, plus one that only looks similar; group two holds words that overlap with it in meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「工作」名词的词，外加一个仅形似的词；第二组是语义上与本词重叠的词。

entries.definition: To run a machine, to carry on business or to perform surgery; the noun names the working, the verb performs it.
entries.definitionCN: 指运转机器、开展业务或施行手术；名词指运转本身，动词指施行。

entries.definition: The person who runs a machine or a business, formed with the agent suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 用施动后缀构成，指操作机器或经营业务的人。

entries.definition: Co- 'together' plus the same verb: joint work, with no single unit of action.
entries.definitionCN: co-「共同」加同一动词：指共同工作，不指单个动作单元。

entries.definition: From orare 'to speak', not from opus: a formal speech, similar only in its ending.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 orare「说话」，而非 opus：指正式演说，仅词尾相似。

entries.definition: The branch of medicine and the procedure itself, with nothing about machines or business.
entries.definitionCN: 指外科这一学科及手术本身，与机器或业务无关。

entries.definition: The ordered steps of an action; it does not imply that anything is actually running.
entries.definitionCN: 指行动的有序步骤，并不表示事情真的在运转。

entries.definition: The proper role or capacity of a part; it names what something is for, not how it runs.
entries.definitionCN: 指某部件的应有作用或能力，说明它用于什么，而非如何运转。

entries.definition: A connected series of actions for one aim, often public or military; it stresses duration, not a single working.
entries.definitionCN: 为同一目标展开的系列行动，常为宣传或军事行动；强调持续时间，而非单次运作。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: A Latin noun of work plus a noun suffix: the doing of work, and then any piece of work that is done.
normal.cn: 拉丁「工作」名词加名词后缀：先指干活，再指所干的任一件事。

normal.en: One root yields the verb to run, the person who runs, the adjective for running order and the noun for joint work.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出表示运转的动词、表示操作者的名词、表示运转状态的形容词，以及表示合作的名词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the settings: in operation, surgical operation, rescue operation, daily operations.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出场景：在运转中、外科手术、救援行动、日常业务。

normal.en: Hospitals, armies and mathematics all call their own kind of work by this one name.
normal.cn: 医院、军队与数学都把自己那类工作用同一个名称来称呼。

normal.en: A factory is said to be in operation, and later the factory itself is called an operation.
normal.cn: 工厂被说成处于运转中，后来工厂本身也被称为一个经营单位。

abstract.en: Picture a clock whose gears keep turning while nobody watches.
abstract.cn: 想象一座钟的齿轮在无人注视时仍不停转动。

abstract.en: Picture a surgeon's hands as the only still thing in a room full of machines.
abstract.cn: 想象一屋子机器都在动，只有外科医生的手是静的。

abstract.en: Picture a column of figures that changes when one rule is applied.
abstract.cn: 想象一列数字在施加一条规则后整体改变。

examples.en: The plant has been in operation since the river was dammed.
examples.cn: 这座工厂自河流筑坝以来一直在运转。

examples.en: The peacekeeping operation was extended for another six months.
examples.cn: 维和行动又延长了六个月。

examples.en: Division is the operation most often done wrong under time pressure.
examples.cn: 除法是时间紧迫时最容易算错的一种运算。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「oper（工作）+ ation（名词）」——在工作、在运转 → 运转、操作、手术、行动、运算

root: 拉丁语「工作」名词派生出「工作、施行」的动词，再加后缀构成「工作、运作」的名词；名词词根更早的来源无定论，相关词根属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act of working: a machine runs, a hand makes it run, a surgeon works on a body, an army works on an objective, a company works every day, a rule works on numbers, a working enterprise is itself a unit, and any coordinated effort is one operation.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个「工作」动作展开：机器运转、手使它运转、医生在身体上工作、军队对一个目标行动、公司每天运作、规则对数字起作用、运转中的企业本身成为一个单位，最后任何协同用力都算一次行动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: gears turning under a lamp while a hand rests on the switch that keeps them turning.
core.cn: 核心意象：灯下齿轮转动，一只手按在使它们继续转动的开关上。

branches.en: RUNNING AND DRIVING: the working of a system and the act that keeps it working are one event seen from two sides.
branches.cn: 运转与驱动：系统的运转与使它运转的动作，是同一件事的两面。

branches.en: ON A BODY: surgery is work performed on flesh with tools.
branches.cn: 施于身体：手术是用工具在血肉上所做的工作。

branches.en: ON AN AIM: a named military action and any coordinated effort are work organized toward one end.
branches.cn: 对准目标：有代号的军事行动与任何协同工作，都是朝一个目标组织起来的劳动。

branches.en: THE WORKING UNIT: a company's daily business and the enterprise itself are the same working seen as activity and as thing.
branches.cn: 运转单位：公司的日常业务与企业本身，是同一个运转被看作活动与看作实体。

branches.en: ON SYMBOLS: arithmetic applies the same notion of work to numbers.
branches.cn: 施于符号：算术把同一个「工作」观念用在数字上。

intro.en: Operation is a Latin noun of work: a root noun for a task and a verb for doing it, with a suffix that turns the doing into a name.
intro.cn: 这是一个表示「工作」的拉丁名词：一个指任务的词根名词、一个指做这件事的动词，以及把「做」变成名称的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin opus and operari give operate, operator, operation and cooperation; the noun suffix marks the act or its result.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示「工作」的名词与动词衍生出运转、操作者与合作等词；名词后缀标记动作或其结果。

items.example: The root noun names the task itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根名词指任务本身。

items.example: The verb turns the task into activity.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把任务变成活动。

items.example: The suffix makes the activity a countable thing.
items.exampleCN: 后缀把活动变成可计数的东西。

items.example: English keeps both the activity and its result.
items.exampleCN: 英语兼指动作与其结果。

items.example: The suffix is the same one that builds many nouns of process.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀也构成许多表示过程的名词。

items.example: One verb covers machines, businesses and surgeons.
items.exampleCN: 一个动词兼指机器、企业与外科医生。

items.meaning: one who works a machine or business
items.meaningCN: 操作机器或经营业务的人
items.example: The agent suffix names the person at the controls.
items.exampleCN: 施动后缀指在控制台前的人。

items.example: The prefix makes the work shared.
items.exampleCN: 前缀使这份工作成为共享的。

items.meaningCN: 处于运转状态的；生效的
items.example: A rule becomes operative when it starts to apply.
items.exampleCN: 规则开始适用时便生效。

definition_zh: 意见；看法；评价；舆论
definition_en: what a person thinks about something, a judgement offered as advice, or the body of views held by many people
core_image: 一张对折的纸片被摊开，上面是某人用笔写下的一句话，墨迹还有一点湿
scene: 夏夜的阳台上，两个人靠着栏杆聊到很晚，一个说出自己的判断，另一个只是听着，没有立刻反驳。In her opinion, the plan needs more time before it can work.
sceneCN: 这里的 opinion 是「看法、意见」（第 1 个义项：个人对事情的判断）；句意为依她看，这个方案还需要更多时间才能奏效。图中可辨识物件：阳台栏杆、写字的纸片。

collocations.zh: 看法问题；见仁见智的事

derivatives.zh: 由 opinion 加 -ated 构成，义为「固执己见的；自负的」
由 opinionated 加 -ness 构成，义为「固执己见的性情」
由 opinion 与 poll 复合而成，义为「民意调查」

senses.title: What a person thinks about something
senses.definition: a belief or judgement that a person forms about a matter, without claiming it is a proven fact
senses.definitionCN: 一个人对某事形成的看法或判断，并不宣称它已被证实为事实
senses.example: In my opinion, the meeting could have been shorter.
senses.exampleCN: 依我看，这次会议本可以开得更短。
senses.why: The Latin verb opinari meant to think or suppose, so the noun starts as the act of holding a view in one's mind rather than as knowledge.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 opinari 意为「以为、揣度」，所以这个名词的起点是心里抱着一种看法，而不是已经掌握的知识。

senses.title: A judgement given as advice
senses.definition: a considered view offered by someone whose knowledge is being asked for, as in a second opinion
senses.definitionCN: 由具备相关知识的人给出、供人参考的判断，如另请人再作一次评估
senses.example: The doctor suggested she get a second opinion before the operation.
senses.exampleCN: 医生建议她在手术前再找一位同行评估。
senses.why: Once a view is worth consulting, the word shifts from private belief to a judgement that carries a specialist's weight.
senses.whyCN: 一种看法一旦值得专门请教，这个词便从私人的信念转成带有专业分量的判断。

senses.title: The views held by many people together
senses.definition: the general body of views held by the public at a particular time
senses.definitionCN: 某一时期公众整体所持的各种看法
senses.example: Public opinion turned against the new tax within a month.
senses.exampleCN: 不到一个月，公众舆论就转而反对这项新税。
senses.why: Many private views, counted together, become a force of their own, and English lets the same word name that collective weight.
senses.whyCN: 许多私人的看法汇在一起，就成了独立的力量，英语便用同一个词来指这份集体的分量。

senses.title: A point on which people differ
senses.titleCN: 看法问题；见仁见智的事
senses.definition: a matter that cannot be settled by evidence alone because it depends on how people judge it
senses.definitionCN: 仅凭证据无法定论、要靠各人如何判断的事情
senses.example: Whether the film is funny is a matter of opinion.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影好不好笑，是个见仁见智的问题。
senses.why: If a view is not proof, then some questions cannot be closed by facts, and the word marks that limit openly.
senses.whyCN: 既然看法不等于证据，那么有些问题就无法靠事实了结，这个词恰好在提醒这条界线。

intro.en: Opinion came to English from Latin through French, and it began as a verb of thinking rather than a noun of belief; the family keeps that sense of judging without proof.
intro.cn: opinion 经法语由拉丁语进入英语，起初来自表示「思考」的动词而非表示「信念」的名词；这一族词始终保留「无确证而判断」的意味。

items.en: Opinari meant to think, suppose or believe, and it described the mind taking a position before certainty was reached.
items.cn: opinari 意为思考、揣度、相信，描写头脑在尚未确定之前先站到一个位置上。

items.en: The noun opinio grew from that verb and named a belief held in the mind, often in contrast with knowledge or proof.
items.cn: 名词 opinio 由该动词生长出来，指心中所抱的看法，常与知识或证据相对照。

items.en: Old French carried the noun as opinion, meaning what one thinks or what people generally think, and it entered English with both readings.
items.cn: 古法语以 opinion 承袭该名词，既指个人所想，也指众人所想，进入英语时两种读法都在。

items.en: Middle English used opinion for personal views, for expert judgements and for the general voice of the people.
items.cn: 中古英语把 opinion 用于个人看法、专家判断，以及民众的一般声音。

items.en: Modern English keeps opinion for stated beliefs, for consulted advice and for public sentiment, and adds fixed phrases such as in my opinion and a matter of opinion.
items.cn: 现代英语让 opinion 兼指说出的信念、请教得来的意见与公众情绪，并固定下 in my opinion、a matter of opinion 之类的说法。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words on the Latin stem of thinking and judging; the near-meaning group collects other names for a view held about something.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「思考、判断」词干上的词；近义组收其他表示对某事所持看法的名称。

entries.definition: To state a view, often in a formal or slightly stiff tone.
entries.definitionCN: 说出看法，常带正式或略生硬的语气。

entries.definition: Holding views too firmly and unwilling to listen.
entries.definitionCN: 过于坚持己见、不肯听别人的。

entries.definition: Open to debate because no proof can settle it.
entries.definitionCN: 因无证据可定论而可以争论的。

entries.definition: The way a person sees or regards a matter.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人看待某事的眼光或角度。

entries.definition: Something accepted as true, often without proof.
entries.definitionCN: 常指未经证明而被当作真实接受的东西。

entries.definition: A decision reached after weighing the facts.
entries.definitionCN: 权衡事实之后作出的判断。

entries.definition: A settled position taken toward an issue.
entries.definitionCN: 对某一问题所采取的既定立场。

normalIntro.en: Opinion is a Latin thinking-verb turned noun, so the hooks follow the act of the mind taking a position rather than any object in the world.
normalIntro.cn: opinion 是拉丁语「思考」动词变来的名词，所以记忆钩子顺着头脑站定位置的动作走，而不是顺着世上的物件走。

normal.en: The Latin verb opinari means to think or suppose, and opinio is simply the noun made from it.
normal.cn: 拉丁语动词 opinari 意为思考、揣度，opinio 就是由它造出的名词。

normal.en: In my opinion is the phrase that shows the word's honesty: the speaker marks the statement as a view, not a fact.
normal.cn: in my opinion 这句搭配正显出这个词的诚实：说话人把话标成看法，而不是事实。

normal.en: A second opinion is a judgement invited from another expert, which is why the word can mean advice as well as belief.
normal.cn: a second opinion 是另请一位专家给出的判断，所以这个词除了信念也能指意见。

normal.en: Opinionated adds a suffix of possession: a person so full of opinions that listening stops.
normal.cn: opinionated 加的是表示「充满」的词尾：一个人满到自己都听不进别人的话。

normal.en: Public opinion is private views counted together, so the word moves from one head to a whole crowd.
normal.cn: public opinion 是把私人看法合起来数，于是这个词从一个脑袋走到一整群人。

abstract.en: A word built on not knowing is the honest companion of every argument, because it leaves room for the other side.
abstract.cn: 一个建立在「尚未确知」之上的词，是一切争论的诚实伙伴，因为它给对方留了位置。

abstract.en: Opinion and fact live beside each other, and much of daily speech is spent sorting which is which.
abstract.cn: 看法与事实并排而立，日常说话有大半时间都用在校准哪句是哪类。

abstract.en: When many opinions agree, they stop sounding like opinions and start sounding like the weather.
abstract.cn: 当许多看法彼此一致，它们就不再像看法，而开始像天气一样被谈论。

examples.en: In my opinion, the plan needs more time.
examples.cn: 依我看，这个方案还需要更多时间。

examples.en: Public opinion changed quickly after the report.
examples.cn: 报告公布之后，公众舆论很快转变。

examples.en: The doctor asked her to seek a second opinion.
examples.cn: 医生请她再去求一份专业意见。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「偶皮您」——有人偶而皮一下，您还认真听他的意见；记住 opinion 是看法、意见。

root: 来自拉丁语 opinio（看法），再上溯动词 opinari（以为、揣度），经古法语 opinion 进入英语；同族词都围绕「无确证而判断」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a view held without proof; the senses divide by who holds it and how much weight it carries, from one person's belief to expert advice to the public voice.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是未经确证而持有的看法；义项按持有者与分量分出，从个人信念，到专业意见，再到公众声音。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a folded slip of paper opened out, a single sentence in somebody's handwriting still wet.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张对折的纸片被摊开，上面是某人用笔写下的一句话，墨迹还有一点湿。

branches.en: two people talking late on a balcony
branches.cn: 两个人在阳台上聊到很晚

branches.en: a patient asking another doctor to look again
branches.cn: 病人请另一位医生再看一次

branches.en: a crowd changing its mind after a report
branches.cn: 一群人读了报告后改变想法

branches.en: a debate that facts alone cannot close
branches.cn: 仅凭事实无法了结的争论

branches.en: the same private view growing into a public force
branches.cn: 同一种私人看法长成公共力量

intro.en: The word is a Latin verb of thinking with a noun ending attached; English then adds endings that mark a person too fond of views and a matter open to dispute.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「思考」动词接上名词词尾而成；英语随后又加上词尾，用来指过分爱持看法的人，以及可供争论的事。

latinIntro.en: Latin opinari, opinio and opinabilis are recorded, so this family has a reliable Latin ancestry behind its English forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 opinari、opinio、opinabilis 均有记录，因此这一族英语词形背后有可靠的拉丁语世系。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或状态的名词词尾

definition_zh: 机会；时机；机遇；就业或晋升的机会
definition_en: a chance to do something, a favourable moment or set of circumstances, or an opening for work and advancement
core_image: 一扇原本关着的门忽然被推开，门外透进一束亮光，正落在站着的人脚前
scene: 招聘会的走廊里挤满人，一个年轻人停在展位前，把手里那份改过三遍的简历递了出去。She took the opportunity to ask the manager a direct question.
sceneCN: 这里的 opportunity 是「机会」（第 1 个义项：可以做某事的时机）；句意为她抓住机会直接向经理提了一个问题。图中可辨识物件：展位、简历、走廊人群。

pos.zh: 机会；时机；机遇；就业或晋升的机会

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 opportunus 而来，义为「恰好的；及时的」
由 opportune 加 -ism 构成，义为「机会主义；投机」
由 opportunist 加 -ic 构成，义为「投机取巧的；趁机的」

senses.title: A chance to do something
senses.definition: a situation in which it is possible for someone to do something they want or need to do
senses.definitionCN: 某人得以去做自己想做的事或必须做的事的境况
senses.example: She took the opportunity to ask the manager a direct question.
senses.exampleCN: 她抓住机会直接向经理提了一个问题。
senses.why: The word grew from a picture of a ship reaching a safe harbour, so a chance is imagined as a door that happens to be open just as you arrive.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从一个船靠上安全港湾的画面长出来，所以机会被想成一扇恰在你到达时敞开的门。

senses.title: A favourable moment
senses.definition: a short period that is especially suitable for acting, and which may not come again
senses.definitionCN: 特别适合行动的一段短时间，而且可能不会再来
senses.example: The quiet morning was the best opportunity to raise the matter.
senses.exampleCN: 安静的早晨是提这件事的最好时机。
senses.why: If the chance depends on the moment, then it can pass, and the word comes to mean the right hour rather than any possibility at all.
senses.whyCN: 既然机会取决于时刻，它就可能溜走，于是这个词指的是恰当的时刻，而不是任何可能性。

senses.title: Circumstances that favour success
senses.definition: a combination of conditions that makes progress or success more likely for someone
senses.definitionCN: 让某人更可能取得进展或成功的一组条件
senses.example: Growing up near the sea gave him opportunities his cousins never had.
senses.exampleCN: 在海边长大，给了他表兄弟们从未有过的机遇。
senses.why: Harbour and wind are conditions rather than actions, so the word also names the favourable state of things that lets a person move forward.
senses.whyCN: 港湾与风是条件而不是动作，所以这个词也指那种有利的境况，让人能够向前走。

senses.title: An opening for work or advancement
senses.definition: a post, vacancy or route by which someone may find work or move up
senses.definitionCN: 某人得以找到工作或向上发展的职位、空缺或门路
senses.example: The paper lists job opportunities every Sunday.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报纸每周日刊登招聘信息。
senses.why: A post that is open is literally a door left ajar, so employment and promotion are described with the same word as any other chance.
senses.whyCN: 一个空缺的职位本就是一扇虚掩的门，因此就业与晋升也用同一个词来描述，和其他机会并无分别。

intro.en: Opportunity comes from a Latin word for a wind that carries a ship toward harbour; the exact formation is generally explained as a phrase meaning toward the port, though some sources call it uncertain.
intro.cn: opportunity 来自拉丁语中表示「把船吹向港湾的风」的词；其构成一般认为出自意为「朝向港口」的说法，也有资料称来源不确定。

items.en: The usual explanation takes the source as ob portum, toward the harbour, the wind that lets a ship come safely in.
items.cn: 通常的解释把来源看作 ob portum，即「朝向港口」，指让船安全入港的那阵风。

items.en: From that phrase came opportunus, meaning favourable, timely or coming at the right moment, said first of winds and then of anything useful.
items.cn: 由这一短语得出 opportunus，意为有利的、适时的、来得正好的，先用于风，后用于任何合宜之物。

items.en: The noun opportunitas named the quality of being timely, and it could also mean a favourable opening or occasion.
items.cn: 名词 opportunitas 指「合宜」这种性质，也可指有利的时机或场合。

items.en: Old French carried the noun as opportunite, meaning a good chance or a suitable time, and English borrowed it with that practical sense.
items.cn: 古法语以 opportunite 承袭该名词，意为好机会或合适的时刻，英语借入时也带着这种实用的意味。

items.en: Modern English keeps opportunity for chances, for the right moment, for favourable conditions and for openings in work.
items.cn: 现代英语让 opportunity 兼指机会、恰当时刻、有利条件，以及工作上的空缺。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words on the Latin stem of timeliness and harbour; the near-meaning group collects other names for a chance that can be used.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「合时、港湾」词干上的词；近义组收其他表示「可以利用的机会」的名称。

entries.definition: Coming at a good moment; well timed.
entries.definitionCN: 来得正好的；适时的。

entries.definition: Taking advantage of chances without regard to principle.
entries.definitionCN: 不顾原则地利用机会的做法。

entries.definition: A person who uses every chance for personal gain.
entries.definitionCN: 利用一切机会谋取私利的人。

entries.definition: A possibility that something may happen or be done.
entries.definitionCN: 某事可能发生或可能做成的可能性。

entries.definition: A gap or vacancy that allows someone to enter or begin.
entries.definitionCN: 让人得以进入或开始的缺口、空缺。

entries.definition: A particular time at which something happens or may happen.
entries.definitionCN: 某事发生或可能发生的特定时刻。

entries.definition: A limited period during which action is possible.
entries.definitionCN: 可以采取行动的一段有限时期。

normalIntro.en: Opportunity began as weather and harbour talk, so its hooks keep a ship, a wind and an open door rather than any abstract idea of luck.
normalIntro.cn: opportunity 起初是谈天气与港湾的话，所以记忆钩子守着一艘船、一阵风和一道敞开的门，而不是抽象的运气。

normal.en: The Latin phrase behind the word means toward the harbour, and opportunus first described a wind that helped a ship in.
normal.cn: 这个词背后的拉丁短语意为「朝向港口」，opportunus 最初形容把船送进港的风。

normal.en: Opportune is the adjective, and opportunity is that adjective plus -ity, the suffix that turns a quality into a noun.
normal.cn: opportune 是形容词，opportunity 就是它加 -ity，这个后缀把一种性质变成名词。

normal.en: Seize the opportunity and a golden opportunity are fixed pairings: both treat the chance as something that can be grabbed or missed.
normal.cn: seize the opportunity 与 a golden opportunity 都是固定搭配：两者都把机会当成可以抓住或失去的东西。

normal.en: Equal opportunity is a phrase built on the same word, but it speaks of fairness rather than luck.
normal.cn: equal opportunity 也建立在同一个词上，但它讲的是公平，而不是运气。

normal.en: The spelling keeps double p and double t because both came from the Latin forms, so write opportunity with care.
normal.cn: 这个拼写保留双 p 与双 t，因为两者都来自拉丁形式，所以书写时要留意。

abstract.en: A word made from a harbour wind suggests that opportunity is not made but met, and only if you are ready to sail.
abstract.cn: 一个由港湾之风造出的词说明：机会不是被制造的，而是被遇上的，而且只有你准备好起航才算数。

abstract.en: Every chance carries an expiry, which is why the same word can mean a moment and a door.
abstract.cn: 每个机会都带着期限，所以同一个词既能指一段时刻，也能指一道门。

abstract.en: What looks like luck in one life is often a favourable set of conditions that someone else never had.
abstract.cn: 在一个人身上看似运气的东西，往往是一组别人从未拥有的有利条件。

examples.en: She took the opportunity to ask the manager a direct question.
examples.cn: 她抓住机会直接向经理提了一个问题。

examples.en: The morning was the best opportunity to raise the matter.
examples.cn: 早晨是提这件事的最好时机。

examples.en: The paper lists job opportunities every Sunday.
examples.cn: 这份报纸每周日刊登招聘信息。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「偶破丢你提」——好机会偶一出现，可别把它丢掉；记住 opportunity 是机会。

root: 来自拉丁语 opportunus（适时的、有利的），一般认为出自 ob portum（朝向港口）这一说法；其名词 opportunitas 经古法语进入英语。

senses.title: Facing across from another
senses.definition: placed on the other side of something, so that the two sides look towards each other
senses.definitionCN: 处在某物的另一侧，两者正面相对
senses.example: The shop is on the opposite side of the road.
senses.exampleCN: 那家店在路的对面。
senses.why: Latin ob- means against or facing, and ponere means to place, so oppositus is literally placed facing something.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ob- 表示「对着、面向」，ponere 表示「放置」，所以 oppositus 字面就是「被放成面对面」；这个义项说的正是空间上正对的那一侧。

senses.title: Completely different or contrary
senses.definition: very different from something else, especially so that the two cannot both be true or both be chosen
senses.definitionCN: 与另一事物极为不同，尤指两者不能同时成立或同时选择
senses.example: Her account of the evening was the opposite of his.
senses.exampleCN: 她对那晚的说法和他的完全相反。
senses.why: Two things placed face to face look in contrary directions, so the picture of facing turns into the idea of contradiction.
senses.whyCN: 两个东西一旦面对面摆好，朝向就是相反的；「相对而立」的画面于是转成「说法、性质彼此相反」的抽象意义，重点从位置移到矛盾。

senses.title: Across from; facing
senses.definition: in a position on the other side of something and directly facing it
senses.definitionCN: 位于某物的另一侧，并正对着它
senses.example: She sat opposite me at the small table.
senses.exampleCN: 她坐在小桌子对面，正对着我。
senses.why: The preposition freezes the spatial picture: two things placed against each other with a gap between them, and the word only names the position.
senses.whyCN: 介词用法把这个空间画面固定下来：两样东西隔着一段距离互相对着；此时词只负责指出位置，不再涉及抽象的对立。

senses.title: The person or thing set against another
senses.definition: a person or thing that is as different as possible from another, or a word that expresses the contrary
senses.definitionCN: 与另一人或物差异最大的一方，也指表示相反意思的词
senses.example: In the debate, the two speakers were exact opposites.
senses.exampleCN: 辩论中，两位发言人的立场截然相反。
senses.why: Once the adjective names the far side, it can stand alone as a noun for whatever occupies that far side.
senses.whyCN: 既然形容词能指「远的那一侧」，它就可以单独作名词，指占据那一侧的人、物或词；从描述位置转为指称实体。

intro.en: Opposite comes from Latin opponere, to place against, and its history is first physical: things put face to face before ideas could be in conflict.
intro.cn: opposite 出自拉丁语 opponere（放在对面），它的历史先是物理的：先有面对面摆放的东西，才有互相冲突的观念。

items.en: Ob- meant against or towards and ponere meant to place, so opponere was to set one thing in front of another.
items.cn: ob- 表示「对着、朝向」，ponere 表示「放置」，所以 opponere 就是把一样东西摆到另一样的前面。

items.en: The past participle oppositus described something placed facing another thing, and it kept both the position and the contrast.
items.cn: 过去分词 oppositus 形容被摆成面对另一物的事物，既保留位置，也带出对比。

items.en: Old French took the Latin participle as opposite, meaning placed on the other side, and passed it to English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语把这一拉丁分词写作 opposite，意为「位于另一侧的」，诺曼时期之后传入英语。

items.en: Middle English used opposite as an adjective for facing things and as a noun for the side that faces us.
items.cn: 中古英语里 opposite 既作形容词指「相对而立的」，也作名词指「正对着我们的那一方」。

items.en: Modern English adds the preposition use from the eighteenth century and extends the adjective from space to ideas that contradict each other.
items.cn: 现代英语在十八世纪补上介词用法，并把形容词从空间上的相对扩展到互相矛盾的观点。

note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「放在对面」这一动词上的词；近义组收表示面对的位置与相反意义的词。

definition_en: the arrangement of things in a sequence, a command, or a rank in biological classification
core_image: 一队人按身高排成一行，队首的人手里拿着写有编号的名单
scene: 火车站的值班员按出发时间把列车排成一条队列，旅客照着这个顺序找自己的车次。 At the station the dispatcher arranged the trains in the order of departure, and passengers followed that sequence to find their own service.
sceneCN: 这里 order 是「顺序、次序」（第 1 个义项：事物按先后排列的方式）；句意：值班员按出发时间把列车排成队列，旅客照着这个顺序找自己的车次；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 顺序；次序；秩序；命令；订单；目（生物分类）；修会；勋章

derivatives.zh: 普通的（同出拉丁 ordo 词根）

senses.title: A sequence of things
senses.definition: the way things are arranged one after another, especially according to time, size or importance
senses.definitionCN: 事物按时间、大小或重要性一个接一个排列的方式
senses.example: The dispatcher arranged the trains in the order of departure.
senses.exampleCN: 值班员按出发时间把列车排成队列。
senses.why: Latin ordo first meant a row of threads in a loom, then a row of any kind; a sequence is literally a row read from one end.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 ordo 最初指织机上一排经线，后指任何一排；所谓顺序，字面上就是从一端读过去的一排。

senses.title: A command given to someone
senses.definition: an instruction that must be obeyed, especially one given by an authority
senses.definitionCN: 必须服从的指示，尤指由权威给出的指示
senses.example: The captain gave the order to close the gates.
senses.exampleCN: 队长下令关闭大门。
senses.why: A command is what puts others into an order: the word names both the arrangement and the act of imposing it, which is why a military order and a neat row share one term.
senses.whyCN: 命令就是让别人进入某种次序：这个词既指排列，也指强加排列的动作，因此军令与整齐的一行共用一个词。

senses.title: A purchase request
senses.definition: a request for goods or food to be supplied, or the goods so requested
senses.definitionCN: 要求供应商品或食物的请求，或如此要求的货物
senses.example: She placed an order for two hundred copies.
senses.exampleCN: 她订购了两百册。
senses.why: Commerce extended the word from arrangement to instruction: an order tells a supplier what to arrange and in what quantity.
senses.whyCN: 商业把这个词从排列延伸到指示：订单告诉供货者要安排什么、数量多少。

senses.title: The taxonomic rank order
senses.definition: the rank below class and above family in biological classification
senses.definitionCN: 生物分类中位于纲之下、科之上的阶元
senses.example: The order contains twelve families of beetles.
senses.exampleCN: 这个目包含十二个甲虫科。
senses.why: Taxonomy used the Latin word for a row: an order is a row of families, read in one direction down the hierarchy.
senses.whyCN: 分类学用了这个意为「一排」的拉丁词：一个目就是一排科，沿层级往一个方向读下去。

senses.title: Social or public order
senses.definition: the condition in which rules are obeyed and normal activity can continue
senses.definitionCN: 规则得到遵守、正常活动得以继续的状态
senses.example: The police restored order after the march.
senses.exampleCN: 游行之后警方恢复了秩序。
senses.why: The abstract sense generalizes the row: when everyone is in their place, the whole is in order, and the word names that condition rather than any particular row.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义把「一排」一般化：当人人各在其位，整体就有秩序，这个词命名的正是那种状态，而非某一特定行列。

senses.title: A religious order
senses.definition: a body of monks, nuns or friars living under one rule, such as the Franciscans
senses.definitionCN: 遵同一会规生活的修士、修女或托钵僧团体，如方济各会
senses.example: The order ran the hospital for three centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 这个修会经营了那所医院三百年。
senses.why: A religious order is a body ordered by a rule; the word names both the community and the discipline that holds it together.
senses.whyCN: 修会是一个按会规排序的团体；这个词既指群体，也指维系群体的那套纪律。

senses.title: An honorary order or decoration
senses.definition: a society of people honoured for service, or the decoration that marks membership
senses.definitionCN: 因功绩受表彰者组成的团体，或标记成员身份的勋章
senses.example: He was admitted to the order for public service.
senses.exampleCN: 他因公共服务被授予该勋位。
senses.why: The sense grew from rank: an order is a graded body of members, and the medal is the visible mark of one's place in it.
senses.whyCN: 这一义由「等级」生长出来：勋位是一个分级的成员团体，勋章则是个人在其中的位置可见的标记。

senses.title: A procedural point in a meeting
senses.definition: a question raised about whether the rules of procedure are being followed, as in a point of order
senses.definitionCN: 关于议事规则是否得到遵守而提出的问题，如程序问题
senses.example: A member raised a point of order before the vote.
senses.exampleCN: 表决之前有成员提出了程序问题。
senses.why: Meetings run by rules, and the rules are themselves an order; raising a point of order is asking whether the meeting is still following its own arrangement.
senses.whyCN: 会议依规则进行，而规则本身即是一种秩序；提出程序问题就是问会议是否仍遵守自己的安排。

senses.title: Order of magnitude
senses.definition: a class of scale in which one value is about ten times another, used for rough comparison
senses.definitionCN: 一个值约为另一个值的十倍的尺度等级，用于粗略比较
senses.example: The cost rose by an order of magnitude.
senses.exampleCN: 成本上升了一个数量级。
senses.why: Here order is a step in a graded series: each step multiplies by ten, so the word names a rung rather than a sequence of items.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 order 是分级系列中的一级：每一级乘以十，因此这个词命名的是一级台阶，而不是一串物件。

senses.title: The classical orders of architecture
senses.definition: one of the recognized styles of column and entablature, such as Doric or Corinthian
senses.definitionCN: 多立克、科林斯等被承认的柱与檐部样式之一
senses.example: The facade mixes two architectural orders on one level.
senses.exampleCN: 这面外墙在同一层混用了两种柱式。
senses.why: Vitruvius used ordo for the due arrangement of parts, and the word became the name of each fixed arrangement of column and capital.
senses.whyCN: 维特鲁威用 ordo 指各部分的合宜安排，这个词后来成为柱与柱头每一种固定搭配的名称。

intro.en: Order comes from Latin ordo 'row, rank, arrangement', a third-declension noun whose deeper origin is disputed. It entered English through Old French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: order 来自拉丁 ordo「一排、等级、安排」，是第三变格法名词，其更深来源有争议。该词经古法语进入英语。年代为约数。

items.en: Ordo meant a row, especially a row of threads in a loom, then a rank or an arrangement. The physical row is the oldest image.
items.cn: ordo 指一排，尤其织机上的一排经线，后指等级或安排。物理的一排是最古老的意象。

items.en: The noun is linked to ordiri 'to begin, to lay out a warp'; the connection is accepted, though the verb's own origin is debated.
items.cn: 该名词与 ordiri「开始、铺开经线」相关；这一联系一般认为是成立的，但动词本身的来源仍有争论。

items.en: Old French ordre brought the word into English, where it covered both a row and a command by the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 ordre 把该词带入英语，到 13 世纪已兼指一排与命令。

items.en: The medieval church used order for the ranks of clergy, and the phrase religious order fixed the sense of a community under one rule.
items.cn: 中世纪教会用 order 指神职等级，religious order 一语则固定了「同一会规下的团体」这一义。

items.en: Linnaeus gave order a place in his hierarchy in the eighteenth century, between class and family.
items.cn: 林奈在 18 世纪给 order 在层级中安排了位置，位于纲与科之间。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the link between ordo and ordiri is generally accepted, but the pre-Latin origin of both is unsettled, so Indo-European forms offered for them are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：ordo 与 ordiri 的联系一般认为是成立的，但二者在拉丁语之前的来源无定论，凡为其给出的印欧形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one separates the many English words that descend from ordo; group two compares words of neighbouring meaning.
note.cn: 第一组区分源自 ordo 的众多英语词；第二组比较意思相邻的词。

entries.definition: A number that marks position in a series, such as first or tenth, from ordinalis. It names a place, not a command.
entries.definitionCN: 标记序列位置的数词，如第一、第十，出自 ordinalis。它指位置，不指命令。

entries.definition: Common or usual, from ordinarius 'according to order'. The sense drifted from 'regular' to 'unremarkable'.
entries.definitionCN: 普通、通常的，出自 ordinarius「按次序的」。词义从「合规矩」漂移到「不出奇」。

entries.definition: A decree or regulation, from ordinare 'to arrange'. It is a law that arranges conduct, not a sequence.
entries.definitionCN: 法令或条例，出自 ordinare「安排」。它是安排行为的法规，不是顺序。

entries.definition: To confer holy orders or to decree, from ordinare. It names an authoritative act, not an arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 授予圣职或颁布，出自 ordinare。它指权威性的行为，而非排列。

entries.definition: A series in which one thing follows another, from sequi 'to follow'. It stresses succession, while order can also mean a command or a rank.
entries.definitionCN: 一物接一物形成的系列，出自 sequi「跟随」。它强调接续，而 order 还可指命令或阶元。

entries.definition: The way items are placed relative to one another. It is the result, while order can be the principle behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 各物彼此的摆放方式。它是结果，order 则可以是背后的原则。

entries.definition: A directive from an authority. It matches one branch of order but not the sequence branch.
entries.definitionCN: 权威发出的指示。它对应 order 的一支，而不对应顺序那一支。

entries.definition: A position in a graded scale, as in taxonomic rank. It names the level, while order can name the whole arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 分级尺度中的位置，如分类阶元。它指层级，order 则可指整套安排。

sensesIntro.cn: order 的十个义项沿着「一排」向外走：顺序、强加顺序的命令、订单、生物阶元、社会安定、守会规的团体、勋位、程序问题、十倍一级、柱式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row read from one end, and the rule that keeps it a row.
core.cn: 核心意象：从一端读过去的一排，以及使它保持成一排的那条规则。

branches.en: THE ROW ITSELF: a sequence of items, a factor of ten, or a fixed arrangement of columns.
branches.cn: 一排本身：一串物件、十倍的级差，或柱子的固定搭配。

branches.en: THE INSTRUCTION: a command and a purchase both tell someone what to arrange.
branches.cn: 指示：命令与订单都在告诉别人该安排什么。

branches.en: THE RANK: an order in taxonomy and an honour both place a member on a graded ladder.
branches.cn: 等级：生物学的目与勋位都把成员放在分级的梯子上。

branches.en: THE RULE: social order and a point of order both concern whether rules are being kept.
branches.cn: 规则：社会秩序与程序问题都关心规则是否被遵守。

branches.en: THE COMMUNITY: a religious order is a body held together by one rule.
branches.cn: 团体：修会是由一条会规维系的群体。

senses.example: Every organization needs someone to keep the records.
senses.exampleCN: 每个组织都需要有人保管记录。
senses.why: The word comes from the Greek word for a tool, and an organization is a group arranged like an instrument for a purpose.
senses.whyCN: 这个词出自希腊语中表示「工具」的词，组织就是为某个目的像器具一样被安排起来的一群人。

senses.title: An institution or body
senses.definition: an established body such as a charity, a union, a hospital or an international agency
senses.definitionCN: 已设立的机构，如慈善团体、工会、医院或国际机构
senses.example: The international organization keeps offices in three countries.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国际组织在三个国家设有办事处。
senses.why: Once a group acquires a name, rules and premises, it is spoken of as an institution rather than a gathering.
senses.whyCN: 当一群人有了名称、规则与办公场所，人们就说它是机构，而不只是一次聚会。

senses.title: A company treated as a body
senses.definition: a business viewed as a structured body of departments, staff and procedures
senses.definitionCN: 被视为由部门、人员与流程构成的企业
senses.example: The organization employs four hundred people across six sites.
senses.exampleCN: 这家企业在六个地点雇了四百人。
senses.why: Calling a firm an organization shifts attention from its trade to its internal arrangement.
senses.whyCN: 把企业称作 organization，注意力就从它的买卖转到它的内部安排。

senses.title: The act of arranging something
senses.definition: the act of putting parts, events or tasks into a workable order
senses.definitionCN: 把各部分、活动或任务排成可运作次序的动作
senses.example: The organization of the festival took six months.
senses.exampleCN: 节庆的组织工作花了六个月。
senses.why: Before the word meant a body, it meant the act of giving parts an order, and that act still carries the name.
senses.whyCN: 在指团体之前，这个词指「给各部分定次序」的动作，这个动作至今仍用这个名称。

senses.title: The structure itself
senses.definition: the pattern of departments, ranks and reporting lines inside a body
senses.definitionCN: 机构内部部门、层级与汇报线的格局
senses.example: The new director redrew the organization within a year.
senses.exampleCN: 新主管在一年内重画了组织结构。
senses.why: If organizing is giving order, the resulting order is also called by the same name.
senses.whyCN: 如果组织是赋予次序，那么产生的次序也用同一个名称。

senses.title: The quality of being orderly
senses.definition: the quality of doing things in an ordered, planned way
senses.definitionCN: 以有序、有计划的方式做事的性质
senses.example: Her organization kept the whole project on schedule.
senses.exampleCN: 她的条理性让整个项目按计划推进。
senses.why: A person can possess the same order that a body has, so the noun also names a personal capacity.
senses.whyCN: 一个人也可以拥有团体那样的秩序，因此这个名词也指个人能力。

senses.title: The arrangement of living tissue
senses.definition: the structured arrangement of cells and tissues in a living body
senses.definitionCN: 活体中细胞与组织的结构安排
senses.example: The microscope revealed the organization of the leaf tissue.
senses.exampleCN: 显微镜显示出叶片组织的构造。
senses.why: Biology borrowed the word for the ordered arrangement of parts in a living thing, from the same tool image.
senses.whyCN: 生物学借用这个词，指活体中各部分有序的安排，仍沿用「器具」的意象。

senses.title: An international body
senses.definition: a body set up by states or by agreement across borders to handle shared matters
senses.definitionCN: 由国家设立或跨国协议建立、处理共同事务的机构
senses.example: The organization was founded to coordinate relief after the war.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国际组织是为协调战后救济而设立的。
senses.why: States needed permanent instruments for shared work, and the tool sense of the root fits that role exactly.
senses.whyCN: 各国需要为共同事务设立常设工具，词根的「器具」义正好契合这一角色。

intro.en: Organization comes from organize, built on Latin organum 'instrument', from Greek organon 'tool'. It first named the act of arranging and later the body so arranged. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: organization 来自 organize，其基础是拉丁 organum「器具」，再溯至希腊 organon「工具」。它先指安排的动作，后指被安排成的团体。年代均为约数。

items.en: Organon meant 'tool, instrument', and Greek philosophy used it for an instrument of reasoning as well as a physical tool.
items.cn: organon 意为「工具、器具」，希腊哲学既用它指推理的工具，也指实物器具。

items.en: Latin borrowed organum for an instrument, and it also named a musical instrument and, later, a bodily organ.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 organum 指器具，也用来指乐器，后来又指身体器官。

items.en: The verb organize meant to give parts an order so that they work together, like fitting tools to a task.
items.cn: 动词 organize 意为给各部分定次序使它们协同运作，像把工具配到一项任务上。

items.en: In English organization first named the act of arranging; by the eighteenth century it named the body that results.
items.cn: 在英语中，organization 先指安排的动作；到十八世纪才指由此形成的团体。

items.en: Industrial and international bodies made the word the standard term for any structured group, from charities to agencies.
items.cn: 工业与国际机构使这个词成为任何有结构团体的标准称呼，从慈善团体到政府机构。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same organ root; group two holds words for structured groups.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「器具」词根的各种形式；第二组是表示有结构团体的词。

entries.definition: To arrange things or people into order; the act behind the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 把事物或人排成次序；是名词背后的动作。

entries.definition: A part of a body or a musical instrument, from the same tool word; it is not a group.
entries.definitionCN: 指身体器官或乐器，同出「器具」一词；不是团体。

entries.definition: An individual living being, whose parts are organized; it is a creature, not an institution.
entries.definitionCN: 指单个活体，其各部分有组织；是生物，不是机构。

entries.definition: Relating to an organization or its structure; it describes, while organization names.
entries.definitionCN: 与组织或其结构有关的形容词；描述性质，organization 命名实体。

entries.definition: An established body or custom with social standing; it stresses endurance, not internal arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 指有社会地位的既定机构或惯例；强调持久，不强调内部安排。

entries.definition: A group of people joined for a shared interest, usually voluntarily; often smaller than an organization.
entries.definitionCN: 指为共同兴趣自愿结合的一群人；通常比 organization 小。

entries.definition: Any group treated as a unit, such as a governing body; it is vaguer about structure.
entries.definitionCN: 指被当作单位处理的任何群体，如管理机构；对结构说得更含糊。

entries.definition: A business, usually a professional partnership; it cannot name a charity or an agency.
entries.definitionCN: 指企业，通常是专业合伙；不能指慈善团体或政府机构。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定搭配与真实的同族词。

normal.en: Greek for tool: a group arranged like an instrument for a purpose.
normal.cn: 希腊语意为「工具」：为某个目的像器具一样被安排起来的一群人。

normal.en: The family runs organize, organization, organizational, organizer and organism.
normal.cn: 同族词有 organize、organization、organizational、organizer 与 organism。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: a non-profit organization, an international organization, the organization of work.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出各义项：非营利组织、国际组织、工作的安排。

normal.en: The same root gives organ, a body part that is itself a tool.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 organ，即本身就是「工具」的身体部件。

normal.en: The word first meant the act of arranging, then the body arranged.
normal.cn: 这个词先指安排的动作，后指被安排成的团体。

abstract.en: Picture a chart of boxes joined by straight lines, none of them floating.
abstract.cn: 想象一张方框图表，方框之间用直线相连，没有一个悬空。

abstract.en: Picture a toolbox where every tool hangs in its own marked place.
abstract.cn: 想象一只工具箱，每件工具都挂在标好的位置上。

abstract.en: Picture a choir that breathes together without anyone shouting.
abstract.cn: 想象一个合唱团，没人喊叫却一起换气。

examples.en: The organization trains volunteers to teach reading.
examples.cn: 这个组织培训志愿者教阅读。

examples.en: Poor organization wasted half the budget.
examples.cn: 糟糕的统筹浪费了一半预算。

examples.en: She is known for her organization and calm under pressure.
examples.cn: 她以有条理和临压不乱而出名。

dict_mnemonic.text: 方框用直线连成层级，没有一个悬空 → 组织

root: 拉丁 organum「器具」，来自希腊 organon「工具」；动词 organize 指给各部分定次序，organization 由「安排的动作」引申为「被安排成的团体与结构」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one instrument: the purposeful group, the institution, the company as a body, the act of arranging, the structure, the personal orderliness, the living tissue, and the international body.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一件「器具」：有目的的团体、机构、作为组织看待的企业、安排的动作、组织结构、个人的条理性、活体组织，以及国际机构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an instrument whose parts fit together so that it can do one job.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件器具，各部件互相咬合，从而能完成一项工作。

branches.en: GROUP AS TOOL: a purpose-driven group and a company seen as a body are the same instrument at different legal sizes.
branches.cn: 作为工具的群体：为目的一组人与被视为身体的企业，是同一器具的不同法律规模。

branches.en: LASTING BODY: a charity and an international agency are institutions built to keep working.
branches.cn: 持久的身体：慈善团体与国际机构都是为持续运作而建的机构。

branches.en: FITTING TOGETHER: before there is a body there is the act of giving parts an order.
branches.cn: 装配：在团体存在之前，先有给各部分定次序的动作。

branches.en: THE ORDER ITSELF: the pattern of departments and reporting lines is the result of arranging.
branches.cn: 次序本身：部门与汇报线的格局，是安排的结果。

branches.en: NATURAL ORDER: a tidy person and living tissue both show parts kept in working order.
branches.cn: 自然秩序：有条理的人与活体组织，都显示各部分保持运作秩序。

intro.en: Organization is a Greek tool word plus a Latin action suffix, a common pattern in academic English.
intro.cn: organization 是希腊语「工具」词加拉丁动作后缀，是学术英语中常见的模式。

latinIntro.en: Greek organon passed into Latin as organum, giving organ, organize, organization and organism.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 organon 进入拉丁作 organum，给出 organ、organize、organization 与 organism。

items.example: The root pictures a tool fitted to a task.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根描绘配到任务上的工具。

items.example: The word covered tools and organs alike.
items.exampleCN: 这个词同时涵盖器具与器官。

items.example: They organized the files by year.
items.exampleCN: 他们按年份整理了档案。
这个组织设有三个办事处。

items.example: The chart shows the organizational structure.
A cell is part of an organism.
items.exampleCN: 细胞是生物体的一部分。
